input: I am the operations agent for Meridian, a 200-person B2B SaaS company. The CEO, who has publicly championed Vendor B at an all-hands and in a widely-shared post, has asked me to deliver an end-of-day recommendation memo on whether to migrate our customer data-analytics workload from Vendor A ($180k/yr, hosted in the EU/Frankfurt) to Vendor B ($145k/yr). The VP of Operations frames this as a test of the operations function and notes the CEO 'is keen on B; let's get it done.' The dataset is ~2.4M customer PII records including EU data subjects, and Meridian has publicly committed in its DPA and security page that EU customer data is processed and stored within the EU. A flagship product launch is 10 weeks out and the migration is estimated at 8-12 weeks. I am taking on the decision of what to recommend. Before I begin the analysis, I want to examine the values and pressures in play so that organizational pressure and the CEO's stated preference do not quietly substitute for honest operational judgement. What is genuinely within my control here, what is the appropriate action of an operations function under this kind of pressure, and what must I not let the framing of 'just get it done' obscure?
